newsitem.title: FRANCE: Nouvelles Frontieres still wants to buy AOM.
newsitem.headline: Nouvelles Frontieres still wants to buy AOM.

text.p: Jacques Maillot, chairman of Nouvelles Frontieres, said on Saturday he was still interested in buying French airline AOM to strengthen the travel company's market position and to get more slots at Orly airport in Paris.
Speaking in a radio interview, Maillot said, "I am unreservedly a candidate...we want to be even stronger in the market."
"We need slots and we need to bring provincial clients to Paris, that's part of our development strategy, and for that reason I'm confirming we're a candidate to buy (AOM)," he told Radio Classique.
AOM, created in 1991 by the merger of Air Outre Mer and Minerve, is owned by the Consortium de Realisation (CDR), a state entity charged with selling former assets of French bank Credit Lyonnais

Maillot also said Nouvelles Frontieres had seen an increase of around 25 percent in the number of its clients since October and a rise in sales of 22 percent during the same period. Maillot said that Nouvelles Frontiers' competitors were also satisfied with sales so far this year.
Maillot first said he wanted to buy AOM in October last year after pulling out of the bidding for French regional airline Air Liberte, subsequently bought by British Airways.
He said on Saturday he had no regrets about not buying Air Liberte, adding that since British Airways had moved into the French market it had put in four billion francs to cover losses.
Maillot also crticised the lack of dialogue between the management, shareholders and workers at BA's French airlines Air Liberte and TAT, to be merged fully later this year.
Cockpit crew at the two airlines have been on an indefinite strike since April 9 protesting against a cost-cutting plan.

"The atmosphere has to change in France so that there are real negotiations, so that strikes are not the final solution, and in this conflict there is no dialogue between management, shareholders and the unions," Maillot said.
